items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: we're going down to see Marty Pay and Daddy O' Dayley down at the studio

ctx.x: So let's go back to Don Before getting you to Chicago.

Well, like I said, he talked me in to it and convinced me, that hey, I wasn't doing nothing; in fact, I just did have a place to lay down. So he said, 'Let's go get your clothes,' and I picked up a few rags I had, and went with him, and went to the Western Union -- he was waiting on some money from his wife, and as soon as he found me, for plane fare and what not.

Well, we went to Western Union and it arrived, and he said come on, and we went down to this ... it wasn't a hotel; it was this new high rise down there on Houston, right off of West Broadway; he was staying with some friends. We stayed there all night until it was plane time the next morning, so I came back to Chicago. I had left Chicago in '56, and here I'm on my way back to play some concerts, and I felt that it was pretty good, as I had a chance to see my mother and grandmother and son and what not.
